title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We meet at 9AM unless one or more people comment wanting to meet at 8AM which is my preferred time. You’re welcome to show up any time but are encouraged to post it so we have a better idea of what to expect for that day. (Those who share the same comment for start time can simply like that comment so we see how many show up for that time without potentially cluttering the comments.)

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll follow my Florida instructor’s method for balanced clinic matches\. This will typically include quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages team clotting\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: 🚶Yanticaw Park Nutley
description:
Let's Walk!!
Meet along Park Drive in Nutley near the Orechio Sports Complex. We'll walk about 3.5 mile through scenic Yanticaw Park, up to Kingsland St. and back. The path is paved and mostly flat.

Please check the event page beforehand in case of any changes. Inclement weather will cancel the walk.

The Yanticaw Park is an Essex County-owned park in Nutley, New Jersey. It is located between Centre Street and Chestnut Street, extending west to Passaic Avenue.

Essex County began purchasing land in 1911 for creation of the park. Wetlands in the park were drained, and a dam was set up to form a lake. The park was completed in 1914. In 1962, the lake, containing a small island was drained and a channel was dug as a continuation of the natural third river from the south.

title: Lego Robotics for Elementary Students
location: RecRoom, 1 Lackawanna Plaza, Ste. 6, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) 
LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. 
In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. 
Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. 
Kids will explore:
• Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components
• Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect)
• Testing, debugging, and iterating designs
• Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas 
Details:
• 60-minute session
• Small-group format
• No prior experience required

20% of seats are reserved for community sponsorship. Families interested in sponsored spots can email info@kineticmindscreative.com
for details.

A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

FABRIC is a welcoming arts and wellness series designed for adults 55+ to foster creativity, connection, and well-being. Hosted by SAIVA at Lackawanna Station in Montclair, this program brings the community together through engaging, beginner-friendly experiences. By engaging this audience, the project preserves cultural heritage, strengthens social networks, and contributes to overall well-being, aligning directly with Essex County’s commitment to arts, culture, and community enrichment. 
Participants can enjoy: 
Gentle chair yoga and meditation sessions to support relaxation and mobility 
Creative art sessions that encourage self-expression 
A warm, social environment focused on building meaningful connections

For Wellness Sessions: 
Take a deep breath… and give your body the gentle care it deserves. 
This welcoming chair yoga and meditation class is thoughtfully designed for seniors who want to feel stronger, more relaxed, and more at ease in their bodies—without getting down on the floor or pushing beyond their limits. Using a sturdy chair for support, you’ll move through simple, low-impact stretches and guided breathing that help improve flexibility, balance, and overall mobility in a safe and accessible way. 
Research shows that chair yoga can enhance strength, reduce joint pain and stiffness, and even improve balance and confidence with movement—helping to lower the risk of falls while supporting everyday activities. 
But this class is about more than movement… it’s about how you feel. 
Through gentle meditation and calming breathwork, you’ll learn simple tools to manage stress, quiet the mind, and reconnect with a sense of inner calm. These practices activate the body’s natural relaxation response, helping to reduce anxiety, improve mood, and support better sleep. 
You’ll leave each session feeling: 
• More grounded and centered 
• Gently stretched and energized 
• Mentally clear and relaxed 
No experience is needed—just come as you are. Every movement can be modified, and you are always encouraged to go at your own pace. 
This is a supportive, feel-good environment where you can move, breathe, and connect—not just with your body, but with a sense of calm, stability, and well-being that carries into your everyday life. 
Because it’s never too late to feel better in your body… and more at peace in your mind.

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

You’re welcome to show up any time but are encouraged to post it so we have a better idea of what to expect for that day. (Those who share the same comment for start time can simply like that comment so we see how many show up for that time without potentially cluttering the comments.)

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll follow my Florida instructor’s method for balanced clinic matches\. This will typically include quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages team clotting\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. title: Spec-Driven Performance
description:

NJ Code and Coffee presents a talk on "Spec-driven Development: Using spec-driven development for production workflows".

AI coding assistants excel at small tasks and isolated features. But when you're building something that spans multiple files and requires upfront planning, they fall apart.

Spec-driven development fixes this. Write the spec first, let the AI build from it, then iterate.
This talk breaks down how to do it in three phases, what tradeoffs you'll hit, and how to start using it
in your next feature.

\*This talk is a part of NJ Code & Coffee's regular monthly meetup.
**Doors open at 2pm, talk starts at 3, arrive early for networking and light refreshments.**
Bring your laptop.

**The Speaker**
[Erik Hanchett](https://www.linkedin.com/in/erikhanchett/) is a developer who creates technical content, build apps, and speak at events around the world about frontend, JavaScript, AI, and the future of modern development. description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This month we will be reading "We Burned So Bright" by TJ Klune. 

"Husbands Don and Rodney have lived a good long life. Together they've experienced the highest highs of love and family, and lows so low that they felt like the end of the world. Now, the world is ending for real. A rogue black hole is coming for Earth and in a month everything and everyone they've ever known will be gone. Suddenly, after 40 years together, Don and Rodney are out of time. They're in a race against the clock to make it from Maine to Washington State to take care of some unfinished business before it's all over. On the road they meet those who refuse to believe death is coming and those who rush to meet it. But there are also people living their final days as best they know how--impromptu weddings, bright burning bonfires, shared meals, and new friends. And as the black hole draws near, among ball lightning and under a cracked moon in a kaleidoscope sky, Don and Rodney will look back on their lives and ask if their best was good enough. Is it enough to burn bright if nothing comes from the ashes?"

title: Native Vector Search in SQL Server 2025: Building AI-Ready Applications
description:
Cloud Data Driven
SQL Server 2025 extends the data platform with native vector search, enabling AI-powered similarity queries directly inside the database. New vector data types and built-in index structures allow efficient storage and querying of high-dimensional embeddings (e.g., from NLP or image models). With optimized Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms and vector indexes, queries achieve millisecond-level response times - even across millions of vectors.

We will explore how vector indexes optimize performance by accelerating similarity searches and reducing resource consumption, while also discussing their limitations - such as index build times, storage overhead, and scenarios where approximate results may differ from exact matches.
Beyond the database engine, you will see how SQL Server 2025 integrates with Azure Foundry and Azure OpenAI Service, enabling embeddings generated by text and image models to be ingested directly into SQL via API calls. This allows developers to build end-to-end pipelines where model outputs are stored, indexed, and queried in real time - without external search infrastructure.

Use cases include real-time personalized recommendations, semantic analytics, and anomaly detection for security scenarios, all running on your proven SQL platform. Seamless integration with Azure hybrid scenarios enables vector search to scale across on-premises and cloud environments, while enterprise-grade features such as role-based access control and Always Encrypted ensure secure handling of sensitive embeddings.

By the end of this session, you will understand how to leverage SQL Server 2025’s native vector search, vector indexes, and AI integration to build scalable, secure, and intelligent applications - while being aware of their trade-offs and best practices for real-world deployments.

description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

**What is Selichot?**  
The Hebrew word selichah means “forgiveness.” The plural form of the word selichah is selichot, a word traditionally used to refer to additional prayers for forgiveness recited during the month of Elul (through Yom Kippur). description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
